## D-2026-10-18-27 — Preserve the fixed degradation as a representation-domain stress protocol

**Decision:** Classify the current fixed 256→128 SAR input pipeline as a controlled composite representation-domain degradation. Do not describe its multiplier as calibrated physical Gamma speckle, and do not change historical fixed tensors or the B1 gate. Before any prospective degradation matrix, resolve the intended frequency cutoff and LR range/clamping policy.

**Evidence:** `scripts/prepare_fixed_degradation.py` reads grayscale PNGs as `uint8/255` and applies the canonical `log` normalization; `MMCANet/src/degradation.py` defines the runtime operator chain. The fixed train/validation manifests set `freq_window_size=64`, downsample to 128, representation-domain looks 2, negative clamp, and `clamp_output=false`. The FFT function reduces the even request to a 63-bin symmetric window (`k=−31…31`); a synthetic response check passed bin 31 and removed bins 32, 40, and 64. A 129-bin symmetric mask preserved bin 40 and bin 64. The 64-bin cutoff is therefore narrower than the conventional 2× Nyquist support, though intentional extra blur has not been ruled out. The looks-2 representation multiplier measured mean 0.99990 and variance 0.49870 over one million seeded draws. `files.csv` metadata show all 1,600 train and 200 validation LR samples exceed 1, with median above-one pixel fractions of 18.13% and 18.20%; no arrays were read for this summary. The data-free degradation/model suite passed 35 tests.

**Reason:** The source is a noisy 8-bit SAR representation with unknown physical calibration, the target is not clean, and the additional multiplier is applied after log normalization. The resulting input distribution is a reproducible synthetic representation stress condition, but its noise cannot be interpreted as a calibrated sensor look count. The unexpectedly narrow passband also changes the effective restoration difficulty relative to a standard ×2 anti-alias limit.

**Consequence:** Keep existing outputs, masks, historical scores, and gates unchanged. Do not launch new degradation or model training until source/target provenance is resolved and a prospective cutoff/range protocol is declared. This does not change the failed B1 conclusion.

## D-2026-10-18-35 — Declare a prospective ×2 cutoff and LR range policy

**Decision:** Preserve the historical 63-bin fixed tensors and all results. For any future standard ×2 representation-domain matrix, use a symmetric 129-bin FFT support (`k=−64…64` on each 256-pixel source axis) before the existing 256→128 bilinear resampling; this reaches the LR Nyquist limit. Treat the historical 64-request→63-bin cutoff as an undocumented legacy choice, not as a validated standard anti-alias cutoff. For the existing representation-domain Gamma stress condition, clamp negative values before applying the multiplier, do not clamp afterward, and allow the shared LR input to exceed 1 without per-image renormalization. This is a controlled representation-domain condition, not a calibrated speckle model.

**Evidence:** `frequency_truncation_degrade` converts an even request of 64 to a conjugate-symmetric 63-bin window (`k=−31…31`). The existing synthetic response audit found bins 32, 40, and 64 removed by that mask, while a 129-bin symmetric mask preserves bin 40 and the 2× Nyquist bin 64. `build_sar_lr_from_physical_degradation` applies the configured non-negative policy before speckle and only clamps the output when `clamp_output=true`; the fixed protocol sets it false. The Gamma multiplier has unit mean before clipping, and metadata for every fixed train/validation LR sample reports a maximum above 1. Clipping that positive tail would therefore alter the declared representation-noise distribution and bias values downward. These are code and sampling-theory facts; no new degradation output was generated.

**Reason:** The original 64-bin value is a requested window count, not a documented physical cutoff. For 2× decimation, the source-grid Nyquist bin is 64; retaining only ±31 imposes additional blur. Because the PNG/log representation is not calibrated SAR intensity or amplitude, the noise condition must remain explicitly representation-domain. A post-noise clamp would make that already controlled condition a different, intensity-dependent truncated distribution.

**Consequence:** This decision is prospective only and does not authorize a new matrix or training run. Keep the source/target provenance blocker, failed B1 gates, and B2 boundary unchanged. Any future physical-domain degradation requires separate source-value and sensor-domain evidence.

## D-2026-10-18-28 — Treat QDFNet as adjacent quality-aware fusion prior art

**Decision:** Record QDFNet as prior art for learned quality-aware optical–SAR feature fusion in object detection. Do not describe generic quality-aware fusion or reliability gating as novel based on this project. Keep the narrower SAR-output restoration question—especially fidelity under geometric mismatch and fallback to a matched SAR-only reconstruction—open and evidence-gated.

**Evidence:** The full [arXiv manuscript](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22447) (posted 2025-12-27) describes DMQA learned-token scores for feature magnitude stability and directional consistency, and OCNF orthogonalized modality features with reliability-weighted channel fusion. Its datasets are SpaceNet6-OTD-Fog and OGSOD-2.0; its reported robustness experiments use whole-modality dropout at rates 0–0.5, with synthetic optical fog for SpaceNet6-OTD-Fog, and report object-detection mAP50/mAP. The paper states that the same dropout rates are used in training, validation, and test. The reviewed manuscript does not report controlled spatial-shift/warp evaluation or SAR-image reconstruction metrics.

**Reason:** Quality assessment and gated cross-modal feature fusion are already applied to optical–SAR inputs in an adjacent task. Detection labels and mAP do not show that a reliability score predicts pixelwise SAR restoration benefit, geometric-error tolerance, or safe fallback.

**Consequence:** Narrow literature and novelty statements accordingly. No new architecture, experiment, or gate change is justified by QDFNet; continue searching primary sources for SAR-output restoration under measured or controlled residual misregistration.

## D-2026-10-18-29 — Keep the Guan near-real SAR release as an unaudited candidate

**Decision:** Record Guan et al.'s GLRT/adaptive-multilooking SAR despeckling resource as a possible external SAR-only reference candidate, not as clean-ground-truth, optical-guidance, or SR evidence. Do not adopt it or start training from the repository description alone.

**Evidence:** The author-uploaded [full paper](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376744726_Robust_SAR_Image_Despeckling_by_Deep_Learning_From_Near-Real_Datasets) describes time-series Sentinel-1 SLC data over three terrain regions, GLRT/adaptive multilooking to create near-real intensity references, and 270 512×512 pairs (250 training, 20 called testing). The linked [author repository](https://github.com/guan-jianjun/SAR-despeckle) instead calls the 20 pairs validation and describes a later 936-pair 256×256 release after curation, containing original intensity, reference, and phase images. It gives no mapping from these crops to the paper split or source patches and says PGD2Net code is unavailable. The repository lists GPL-3.0, but no data-specific license was established. The linked [Drive archive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1p4w7WNPiqvK2haz53uNqy_ewubcoshle/view?usp=sharing) exposed a sign-in page only through the available interface; no archive or imagery was accessed. The official [IEEE record](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10368288) blocked extraction in this review, so technical details were checked against the author-uploaded manuscript and repository.

**Reason:** A multilooked GLRT reference is a near-real algorithmic target rather than an independent clean observation. The split-label discrepancy and absent crop/source mapping prevent a defensible held-out evaluation, while unresolved stack membership, registration, radiometric domain, and licensing limit safe reuse. The resource contains no optical input or SR target.

**Consequence:** Keep it as an unaudited candidate. Before any SAR-only use, inspect an authorized archive and metadata for target construction, split/group lineage, representation, registration, and license. This does not change local B1/B2 gates, authorize training, or justify accessing project test data.

## D-2026-10-18-30 — Classify MOCEM metadata-conditioned restoration as SAR-only adjacent prior art

**Decision:** Treat De Paepe et al.'s CAID 2025 paper as full-text-reviewed simulation-driven joint SAR despeckling/sidelobe-reduction prior art. It is not optical-guided restoration or SAR super-resolution evidence.

**Evidence:** The [author full text](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.01541) describes MOCEM tuples containing observed complex SLC, an intermediate signal, scene reflectivity, and acquisition metadata. It reports 5,000 256×256 tuples split 4,631/369 across acquisition-parameter ranges; the best metadata-conditioned SEDRUNet reports 30.461 dB PSNR and 0.901 SSIM on simulated validation. The paper calls reflectivity an effective ground-truth candidate, notes that inserted CAD objects receive more faithful scattering simulation than contextual background maps, and shows real Umbra/Capella results with ENL and qualitative evidence but no quantitative sidelobe metric. No public code/data link was identified in the reviewed text.

**Reason:** The paper is relevant to SAR observation modeling and joint restoration, but the target is not physically measurable clean truth, the data are primarily simulated, and the method has no optical input or SR task.

**Consequence:** Include it in related-work and simulation-domain limits. It changes no local experiment gate, optical-usefulness conclusion, or method decision.

## D-2026-10-18-31 — Keep SARLO-80 as an unaudited real-SLC geometry candidate

**Decision:** Do not adopt SARLO-80 as a restoration benchmark or download its shards for the current research track. Keep it as a possible future geometry-diagnostic source pending versioned release and optical-pairing audit.

**Evidence:** The [paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.20523) reports 119,566 Umbra SICD/optical/text triplets, pass-disjoint train/validation/test splits, and affine optical projection from crop-corner correspondences. The current [ONERA Hub card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ONERA/SARLO-80/blob/main/README.md), [reconstruction guide](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ONERA/SARLO-80/blob/main/README_OPTICAL_RECONSTRUCTION.md), and `dataset.yaml` describe optical PNGs as absent and reconstructable on demand, and the visible release exposes only a train split. The guide assigns provider-term checks to users; the card identifies CC-BY-SA-4.0 for SARLO-80, while the paper identifies Umbra SAR as CC-BY-4.0 and Google Satellite TMS as the optical tile source. A historical pinned card revision [b64a605](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ONERA/SARLO-80/blob/b64a605d65aa7f4a63a32b0b2923e3a4f034e29c/README.md) reports 76,448 pairs and lists an optical PNG, unlike the current card and paper storage description. The reviewed sources give no exact optical acquisition dates or quantitative registration residuals.

**Reason:** Complex SLC and geometry metadata could support real-SAR alignment diagnostics, but the current data do not provide a clean reference or restoration LR/HR pair. Split/schema/count history, optical reproducibility and usage terms, and geometric residuals are not resolved.

**Consequence:** Keep it as a candidate only. Before a diagnostic, pin an authoritative split/group manifest, reconcile the release version, check provider terms, and quantify residual registration on permitted samples. No B1/B2 gate changes, model training, project-test-data access, or shard download is authorized by this record.

## D-2026-10-18-32 — Do not treat B1F zero optical as SAR fallback

**Decision:** Record the trained B1F zero-optical path as an observed negative-transfer condition, not as a SAR-only fallback. Do not change B1/B1F gates or start another fusion screen from this diagnostic.

**Evidence:** In the existing `phase_b1f_pairing_diagnostic_20261016_v1` run, the all-zero optical condition was evaluated on the same 200 `fixed_val_dev2k` identities as the SAR-only frozen decoder base. Missing-minus-SAR-only PSNR was `−0.014729 dB` with paired bootstrap 95% CI `[−0.021834, −0.007967]`; all eight recorded metric contrasts moved adversely. The diagnostic manifest records `training_performed=false`, `checkpoint_selection_performed=false`, `test_set_used=false`, and `test_set_accessed=false`. A source-only audit found that the 3×3 matcher always softmaxes across nine optical offsets, B1F adds an unconstrained feature correction at decoder `F60`, training uses final-output SmoothL1, and inference does not bypass fusion when optical is zero.

**Reason:** Zero-initialized identity at initialization does not establish the trained model's missing-optical behavior. The saved paired result directly shows a difference from the SAR base for this checkpoint, but cannot identify cause, generalize across seeds, establish calibrated recovery, or validate a different fallback mechanism.

**Consequence:** Keep the failed promotion status and B2 boundary unchanged. Describe this as one-checkpoint development-validation evidence only. Continue resolving source/target provenance and the declared degradation bandwidth/range policy before proposing another model experiment; do not access test imagery or measurements.

## D-2026-10-18-33 — Do not attribute B1F failure only to final-epoch checkpoint choice

**Decision:** Keep B1F failed and stop at the declared B1F boundary. Do not reselect an inner-dev epoch or rerun the same screen.

**Evidence:** The saved 10-epoch seed0 trajectory has ΔSSIM below zero at every epoch and TBR error change above the `+0.005` cap at every epoch. Epoch 7 reaches the largest PSNR gain (`+0.021866 dB`) but still has ΔSSIM `−0.000458` and TBR error change `+0.022939`; the final epoch has `+0.019419 dB`, `−0.001381`, and `+0.021978`, respectively. The training source marks the saved checkpoint rule as `final_epoch_no_inner_dev_checkpoint_selection`. Per-epoch metric and attention files contain the 160 `inner_dev` names and false test-access flags.

**Reason:** The PSNR-only peak does not satisfy the multi-metric gate, so epoch selection cannot repair the observed screen without changing the declared criterion. The trajectory indicates metric trade-offs under this training setup, but does not identify whether the cause is loss design, feature matching, pseudo-target noise, or training budget. The attention summaries are not a reliability measure.

**Consequence:** Preserve historical results and gates. Keep the local optical-fusion route paused while the source/target and degradation-policy questions remain open. The next method decision must use a new, prospective question rather than reusing this inner-dev trajectory to choose a checkpoint.


## D-2026-10-18-34 — Keep STRATA-S12 as a provenance/geometry candidate only

**Decision:** Do not treat STRATA-S12 as a SAR restoration benchmark or use it to reopen local optical-fusion training. Keep it as a future metadata/geometry candidate pending a versioned subset and source audit.

**Evidence:** The [author preprint](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17680) and [official Hugging Face card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/chsanleo/strata-s12) describe 740,746 co-grid S1/S2 pairs at 512×512/10 m with at most a three-day acquisition gap and per-pair source/acquisition sidecars. The paper’s sidecar schema says S2 dtype `uint16`, while the card says `float32`. The 2.91 TB full release is access-gated; the paper mentions `D_lite`, whose official files were not inspected. A secondary [NLM catalog search result](https://datasetcatalog.nlm.nih.gov/dataset?q=0003343977) reports 740,847, but its direct record could not be opened.

**Reason:** Shared grid and temporal pairing are not a measured residual-registration bound. The reviewed sources provide neither a degraded-SAR/HR-SAR restoration pair nor an independent clean SAR reference, and the stored-value mapping and release/version discrepancies are unresolved.

**Consequence:** Keep it as a candidate only. Before any geometry use, verify authorized files, version, dtype/value mapping, terms, sidecars, source-group splits, and residual alignment. This review changes no B1 gate, B2 boundary, or current pause on local optical-fusion development.

## D-2026-10-18-35 — Keep STRATA-S12 `D_lite` pending record-lineage verification

**Decision:** Treat `D_lite` as author-reported open and potentially inspectable, but do not use or characterize its actual contents until the Zenodo record and files are retrieved and version-pinned. Keep STRATA-S12 as a provenance/geometry candidate, not a restoration benchmark.

**Evidence:** The [author preprint](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17680) says `D_lite` is openly available under CC BY 4.0 as eight per-class archives plus per-pair sidecars, a manifest, checksums, helper script, and examples, and cites DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22646276`. A secondary [NLM catalog entry](https://datasetcatalog.nlm.nih.gov/dataset?q=0003343977) indexes `D_lite` under `10.5281/zenodo.22646277` and reports 740,847 pairs for the full corpus; the paper and current [Hugging Face card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/chsanleo/strata-s12) report 740,746. The paper cites full-corpus DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22699046`, while the card cites `10.5281/zenodo.22699047`. Direct Zenodo page/API routes were not retrievable through this review interface, so no manifest or files were inspected.

**Reason:** The apparent open subset could supply source-scene identifiers and acquisition dates useful for a group/provenance audit, but the observed DOI/count differences prevent reliable attribution to a specific release. Even if the subset is retrieved, the corpus has no paired SAR restoration target and reported common-grid placement is not a measured residual-registration bound.

## D-2026-10-18-36 — Do not carry B1F matcher entropy forward as a global utility cue

**Decision:** The B1F nine-offset matcher-entropy confidence is not supported as a global optical-utility or rejection cue on the current checkpoint and fixed development-validation data. Do not fit a threshold or change B1/B2 gates from this result.

**Evidence:** A no-training Level-0 diagnostic reused the failed B1F seed0 checkpoint and saved per-image metrics for 200 fixed validation identities. The cue was `1 − mean spatial normalized entropy` of the correctly paired nine-way offset weights. Its Spearman associations with eight oriented matched-minus-SAR-only utilities were: PSNR `+0.156`, SSIM `+0.108`, EPI `+0.098`, edge ratio proximity `+0.107`, TBR error reduction `+0.016`, bright-peak ratio proximity `+0.212`, bright-energy ratio proximity `−0.094`, and bright-region MAE reduction `−0.094`. The predeclared all-eight-positive direction rule failed. See the [protocol and results](../../experiments/dev2k_formal/phase_b1f_matcher_entropy_utility_20261018_v1/summary.json) and [optical analysis](optical_information_analysis.md).

**Reason:** More concentrated correspondence weights did not consistently rank benefit across the full metric set; TBR association was near zero, and two bright-region associations had the opposite sign. The image-bootstrap intervals are descriptive because source grouping is unknown. The checkpoint failed its inner-dev gate, `fixed_val_dev2k` has been repeatedly used, the targets are noisy PNG-derived pseudo-targets, and several outcomes use target-derived masks. This is evidence against this particular cue in this setting, not against every possible inference-time reliability cue.

**Consequence:** Do not use matcher entropy as a global utility or rejection signal for this method/data. No training, metric recomputation, checkpoint selection, threshold fitting, or test-set access occurred. B1 remains failed, B2 remains gated, and the broader optical-fusion pause and source/target provenance requirements remain unchanged.

## D-2026-10-18-37 — Keep local SEN1-2 provenance unresolved after metadata-export attempt

**Decision:** Do not treat the local numeric filenames as linked to upstream SEN1-2 scenes or patches. Keep acquisition timing, parent-scene grouping, product lineage, and residual registration unresolved until a source manifest or reliable crosswalk can be inspected.

Attempts to open SEN1-2 record `1436631` and its JSON/CSV export routes through the available web interface returned inaccessible-tool errors. A previous direct record fetch returned HTTP 429. No metadata, archive inventory, or imagery was retrieved.

**Reason:** The local manifests contain numeric identities and hashes but no upstream source identifiers. An inaccessible export route cannot establish that metadata is missing at the source, and matching normalized PNG appearance or numeric order would not provide a defensible crosswalk.

**Consequence:** Keep the provenance action open and retry only from a reachable or authorized source. No dataset was downloaded, no local or test imagery was opened, and no experiment gate or data interpretation changed.

## D-2026-10-19-01 — Classify MLOG as training-time optical-guided SAR SR

**Decision:** Record the Research Square MLOG v1 preprint as optical-guided SAR super-resolution prior art with paired optical supervision during training and SAR-derived pseudo-optical input at inference. Do not classify it as true optical-at-inference restoration or joint despeckling/SR, and do not transfer its protocol to the similarly titled 2025 JARS record.

**Evidence:** The [Research Square record](https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-1687789/v1) identifies the preprint as version 1 and not peer reviewed; a matching [public full-text copy](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361028323_Optical_Image_Guided_Multi-scale_Learning_for_Synthetic_Aperture_Radar_Image_Super-resolution) was reviewed on 2026-10-19. It specifies paired HR optical during training, then bicubic-upsampled and channel-expanded LR SAR as pseudo-optical input at test. The experiment section reports BM3D-prefiltered SEN1-2 “summer” data with 800 train and 10 test pairs. Table 1 reports 45.89 dB/0.993 PSNR/SSIM at ×2; Table 5 reports 45.86 dB/0.993 for its “w/o Optical” model. The protocol does not specify a group split, per-image uncertainty, or controlled registration-error test.

**Reason:** The actual test input and SAR preprocessing limit what the paper establishes: it neither tests access to real HR optical during inference nor evaluates denoising from speckled input. Its reported ×2 optical-ablation difference is small and SSIM is unchanged, while the only independent test set described has 10 pairs.

**Consequence:** Use MLOG to narrow optical-guided SAR-SR novelty claims, while keeping the current B1 failure, B2 gate, and no-training status unchanged. Keep the 2025 journal record separate until primary full text establishes its method and relationship, if any.

## D-2026-10-19-02 — Keep MLOG journal lineage provisional

**Decision:** Keep the 2025 *Journal of Applied Remote Sensing* article as a separate record with a provisional likely connection to the 2022 MLOG preprint. Do not treat them as a verified preprint/journal pair or transfer the preprint's protocol/results.

**Evidence:** J-GLOBAL's [article record](https://jglobal.jst.go.jp/en/detail?JGLOBAL_ID=202502251820438923) displays a JST machine-translated abstract that names MLOG and OWG/MLN/RMB, matching the 2022 preprint's method labels. The journal record lists a fourth author, Yi Xiao. The official [DOI page](https://doi.org/10.1117/1.JRS.19.026506) and SPIE full-text route were inaccessible through the current web interface; the [ResearchGate record](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391339278_Multiscale_learning-based_optical_image-guided_super-resolution_network_for_synthetic_aperture_radar_image) reports no full text available.

**Reason:** The shared method name and module sequence are secondary-abstract evidence and make a relationship plausible, but they do not establish whether the journal article is a revision, continuation, or separate work. The primary article is needed to verify lineage and protocol.

**Consequence:** Retain separate literature-matrix rows and the open primary-text action. No method choice, novelty claim, or B1/B2 gate changes.

## D-2026-10-19-03 — Classify Ka-SAR as SAR-only integrated restoration prior art

**Decision:** Record Zhu et al.'s Ka-SAR article as prior art for integrated SAR speckle suppression and ×4 super-resolution. Do not classify it as same-scene optical-guided restoration or evidence for optical mismatch reliability.

**Evidence:** The IEEE DOI is `10.1109/JSTARS.2025.3606890`; the public [author-manuscript copy](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395373423_Ka-SAR_Image_Super-Resolution_With_Integrated_Speckle_Suppression_via_Generative_Adversarial_Network) was reviewed. Its described SAR generator takes LR SAR at inference. External optical imagery contributes hybrid training examples and feature cues; the manuscript reports higher feature similarity for natural surfaces than roads/buildings. Its simulated comparison is reported slightly below SRNO, and real strip-map results have no pixelwise HR reference.

**Reason:** This is direct overlap with the broader joint-restoration task and narrows novelty claims. Its sensor band, ×4 bicubic task, hybrid training construction, and no-reference real-data evidence differ from the local ×2 noisy-LR/pseudo-target protocol. The terrain screen measures feature similarity for data selection, not local optical usefulness or safe fallback.

**Consequence:** Include it in the literature review and related-work matrix. Keep local B1 failed, B2 gated, and optical-fusion training paused. No code, data, or test artifacts were accessed for this review.

## D-2026-10-19-04 — Keep STRATA-S12 D_lite as a provenance candidate only

**Decision:** Pin D_lite to the inspected Zenodo v1.0.0 record and treat it as an inspectable provenance/geometry candidate, not a SAR restoration benchmark. Do not infer residual registration accuracy from nominal geotransforms or three weak cross-modal probes.

**Evidence:** The [D_lite version record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22646277) is version 1.0.0, published 2026-09-07, open CC BY 4.0; its concept DOI is `22646276`. The full-corpus record's `22699046`/`22699047` pair has the same concept/version distinction. Its 20,916-row manifest has no split and repeats tile/S1/S2 source IDs. Three example pairs share exact nominal grids and pass sidecar byte-hash checks, but SIFT yields too few inliers and gradient correlations are weak. Sample S2 dtype/nodata metadata conflicts with the rasters; exact value transformation is not established. See the [audit report](strata_s12_dlite_audit.md).

**Reason:** The public subset can improve source metadata and reveal split risks, but it provides neither an independent clean SAR target nor a paired restoration target/degradation. Three examples cannot support a release-wide alignment claim, and the optical sidecar/raster discrepancy limits radiometric interpretation.

**Consequence:** Keep D_lite out of restoration comparisons and do not change the local B1 failure, B2 gate, or optical-training pause. If a future geometry study adopts it, first resolve value/nodata semantics and use broader samples with independent tie points and source/spatial grouping.


## D-2026-10-19-05 — Preserve HSFMamba as direct joint-task prior art; keep its noise/code limits explicit

**Decision:** Keep HSFMamba classified as direct optics-guided joint SAR SR/denoising prior art. Do not use the paper's `Gamma` label as evidence of a physically parameterized speckle model or treat the linked resource repository as a reproducible model implementation.

**Evidence:** The [IEEE record](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11045185/) and accessible [author manuscript](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392843218_HSFMamba_Hierarchical_Selective_Fusion_Mamba_Network_for_Optics-Guided_Joint_Super-Resolution_and_Denoising_of_Noise-Corrupted_SAR_Images) describe the joint task and OGSSR data. The manuscript reports `L`-indexed Gamma-noise severity, but no accessible sampling equation/domain/multiplicative convention; it also describes acquisition-time/resolution transforms and moving-target alignment challenges without residual-registration measurements. The [paper-linked GitHub resource](https://github.com/mmic-lcl/Datasets-and-benchmark-code) and [author catalog](https://chenglongli.cn/Datasets-and-benchmark-code/) list OGSSR data but no HSFMamba model-code entry.

**Reason:** The paper is already direct task overlap, while the missing noise construction and model code prevent faithful protocol reconstruction and limit physical/noise comparisons. The alignment discussion further shows that a “well-aligned” dataset label does not itself quantify residual error.

**Consequence:** Retain HSFMamba as strong prior art; preserve those protocol limits in the literature matrix. Do not change local B1/B2 status or start training. Revisit implementation/noise details only if new author or publisher materials appear.

This verifies the public access route and its current gate, not the archive contents or terms.

**Consequence:** Keep OGSSR as a literature-level candidate only. Resume the data audit if an inspectable listing, author-provided metadata, or an accessible mirror appears. Do not change local B1/B2 status or start training.

## D-2026-10-19-07 — Retire current development partitions from independent validation

**Decision:** Treat the fixed train/validation and B1F fit/inner-dev partitions as spatially and target contaminated. Preserve all historical measurements and gate decisions, but do not use these partitions for independent generalization claims or future model selection/promotion. Do not start another model experiment until source-group provenance is recovered or a new prospective development split is independently verified.

**Evidence:** An exhaustive scan of all 1,800 fixed train+validation source images found the same 580 exact cross-split neighbor pairs in SAR and RGB optical. Each pair shares a byte-exact 51×256 or 52×256 source strip, and the corresponding fixed target strips are exactly equal. All 200 validation identities and 510 train identities participate. The B1F train-only overlap graph crosses its 1,440/160 fit/inner-dev partition in 440 exact target geometries, affecting 159 inner-dev identities and 392 fit identities. The six overlap-connected components do not recover original scene, tile, or acquisition IDs. Audit outputs state `test_set_used=false` and `test_set_accessed=false`; no test data was read.

**Reason:** These exact shared target pixels mean the held development identities are not independent of fitting data. The audit establishes contamination but does not estimate its effect on saved scores, so historical values must remain intact and retain their recorded outcomes with the additional limitation.

**Consequence:** Keep B1 failed and B2 gated; no promotion or new local 2k validation-based selection. Recover authoritative source groups or define a new prospective group-disjoint split with spatial-overlap verification before resuming model work. See the [audit report](sen1_2_train_val_spatial_overlap_audit.md).

The official CNIPA query portal was reachable, but the item-specific publication, applicant/status, and complete claims were not independently retrieved. Follow-up exact-number queries restricted to CNIPA and WIPO, plus a Google Patents search, returned no item-level record.

See the [literature review](literature_review.md), [related-work matrix](related_work_matrix.csv), and [research gaps](research_gaps.md).

## D-2026-10-19-09 — Revalidate aligned optical only on a new source-group split

**Decision:** Keep the recorded B1 result failed and unchanged. If provenance is recovered, treat any aligned-optical re-evaluation on a new group-disjoint split as a separate prospective B1 screen; do not reuse old checkpoints or call it a retroactive promotion.

**Evidence:** The current B1 config binds the screen to `fixed_train_dev2k` (1,600) and `fixed_val_dev2k` (200), declares seeds 0–2, and sets a mean paired PSNR threshold of +0.05 dB plus SSIM/EPI/structure guardrails. The exhaustive overlap audit found 580 train/validation source and target overlap geometries and 440 B1F fit/inner-dev target-overlap geometries. Source-group identities are still unrecovered. See the [B1 config](../../configs/dev2k_formal/phase_b1_aligned_optical_gain.json) and [overlap audit](sen1_2_train_val_spatial_overlap_audit.md).

**Reason:** The current validation cannot support new selection or promotion, and a pre-existing SAR-only checkpoint may have trained on identities assigned to a future validation group. A fair new comparison therefore requires matched methods trained only on the same newly frozen fit groups. Correlated patches within a source scene also require uncertainty summaries that resample source groups, not just individual patches.

**Consequence:** After mapping local IDs to upstream scene/ROI paths, freeze a new group-disjoint split using non-test development data, report realized group/sample counts, and run a three-seed matched SAR-only vs aligned-optical screen with the registered thresholds and guardrails. ## D-2026-10-19-10 — Verify local SEN1-2 release identity before applying TUM groups

**Decision:** Treat the project's approximately 20,000-pair “complete data” count as a project-reported local corpus count with unresolved lineage. Do not call it the complete official SEN1-2 release or assume that the TUM ROI/scene hierarchy identifies local samples until the release or derivative is verified.

The local train/validation exact SHA-512 crosswalk found zero byte-identical files among 3,600 checked PNGs; that result excludes byte-identical copies but does not rule out a selected subset, re-encoding, or other transformation. A bounded search within `data/` found no non-PNG sidecar/manifest files that identify the release; image contents and measurements were not opened. A filename-only `rg --files` search for common archive extensions found only the existing B1F review snapshot; its [manifest](../../review_packages/phase_b1f_minimal_review_2026-10-16/REVIEW_MANIFEST.json) excludes raw data, so it is not the missing dataset archive. No local source/version manifest has been recovered.

**Reason:** The project-reported ~20k count, the official 282,384-pair release, and the local 2k subset are not reconciled. Resolving the location and identity of the larger project corpus is necessary before using upstream ROI/season and `s1_i`/`s2_i` folders as source-group labels.

**Consequence:** Locate and recover the ~20k corpus's source URL/archive/version or subset-generation record first, then map only permitted non-test train/validation files to authoritative source paths. Keep current splits, historical measurements, failed B1 status, and B2 gate unchanged; do not access test data or start training on the contaminated partitions.

**Decision:** Refer to the available 2k files as the “project-labeled SEN1-2 subset” until their upstream source is verified. Treat the project’s ~20k SEN1-2 statement as unresolved; do not attribute the local files to QXS-SAROPT based on count alone.

The original [QXS-SAROPT paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.08259) reports a distinct 20,000-pair collection from 1 m single-polarization Gaofen-3 SAR and Google Earth optical across three port cities, and explicitly distinguishes it from SEN1-2. This makes label/count conflation plausible but does not identify this repository's local files. The inventory confirms 2,000 same-named local SAR/optical PNGs; no ~20k image tree or shallow source manifest was found in the inspected `data/` paths. The crosswalk against SEN1-2 found no byte-identical matches.

**Additional geometry evidence:** The local spatial-overlap audit found 51/52-pixel exact shared strips at 204/205-pixel translations, about 20% of a 256-pixel patch. That matches QXS-SAROPT's stated overlap ratio, while SEN1-2 reports 128-pixel stride/50% overlap. QXS's “stride 52” wording is ambiguous under the conventional step-size definition. This makes QXS or another 20%-overlap derivative a stronger hypothesis, not a source assignment; direct provenance is still missing. See the [overlap report](sen1_2_train_val_spatial_overlap_audit.md).

**Reason:** Dataset naming and nominal pair count are insufficient provenance. SEN1-2 and QXS-SAROPT have different sensors, resolutions, geographies, and acquisition/registration protocols, so attributing a local subset to either changes the scientific claims and valid grouping schema.

**Consequence:** Locate the source archive or subset-generation record for both the project-reported ~20k collection and the local 2k files. Until then, preserve historical labels in their original run records but qualify current descriptions as project-labeled; use TUM groups only if SEN1-2 lineage is demonstrated. Do not access test imagery/measurements or start model training on the contaminated partitions.

## D-2026-10-19-18 — Keep SAR-to-EO flow papers as adjacent prior art

**Decision:** Add ReFlowSET and ContraFM-S2O to the generative literature review, but do not treat either as evidence for optical-guided SAR reconstruction or as a direct baseline for the local task.

**Evidence:** The two 2026 arXiv papers use SAR input and EO output. ReFlowSET uses conditional latent flow matching with training-only EO feature alignment and reports a downstream QXS 16,001/3,999 split; ContraFM-S2O uses average-velocity flow matching with contrastive regularization and reports a QXS split of approximately 4:1. Neither paper establishes SAR-output fidelity, despeckling, optical-conditioned SAR inference, or SAR fallback. Full primary-source reviews are recorded in the [literature review](literature_review.md#sar-to-eo-flow-matching-adjacent-reverse-direction-work) and [diffusion feasibility note](diffusion_feasibility.md#flow-matching-work-in-the-reverse-sar-to-eo-direction).

**Reason:** Flow matching is now active in adjacent SAR–EO generation research, but the conditioning/output direction and fidelity objective differ from SAR restoration. Reusing those methods without changing the scientific target would answer a different question.

**Consequence:** Keep the conditional residual-flow idea as a deferred candidate only. Any future local flow experiment still requires a valid target, a source-group-disjoint development split, a matched SAR-only control, scatterer/fidelity checks, and available compute; the current B1/B2 gates do not change.

## D-2026-10-19-22 — Keep CRDRS as reverse-direction residual-diffusion prior art

## D-2026-10-19-23 — Treat Ma et al. as adjacent label-misalignment prior art

**Decision:** Classify Ma et al.'s flood-mapping work as downstream label-misalignment and SAR-only despeckling prior art. Do not use it as evidence for optical-guided SAR restoration, optical rejection/fallback, or the local source-group split.

## D-2026-10-19-25 — Classify Capella SR as real-source, synthetic-degradation evidence

It does not report source-scene grouping, image product/polarization, or a dataset/code release. The article is CC BY 4.0, which does not establish a license for the underlying Capella data. No imagery, split identities, or local test measurements were accessed.

**Reason:** Actual SAR source pixels do not make bicubic-generated LR/HR pairs equivalent to measured cross-resolution sensor observations. Splitting after patch extraction without a source-group protocol leaves geographic independence unresolved. The paper's task is single-modality SR and has no joint despeckling, optical guidance, or fallback test.

**Consequence:** Keep it as prior art for real-source/synthetic-degradation SAR SR. Do not use it as an optical-guided or joint-restoration baseline, a proof of real sensor-resolution generalization, or evidence that the local dataset may be redistributed. B1 remains failed and B2 gated. See the [full review](literature_review.md#sar-super-resolution-and-joint-restoration) and [risk record](RESEARCH_RISKS.md).

## D-2026-10-19-28 — Record posterior-sampling and consistency-model prior art

## D-2026-10-19-31 — Keep joint and physics routes as testable hypotheses

**Decision:** Make joint-versus-cascade performance and SAR observation-model consistency explicit as open, falsifiable research hypotheses. Do not presume that joint restoration is superior or that a physical forward model is validated for the local PNG data.

**Evidence:** Phase-A2 Case B reports 17.3751 dB for its strongest `cnn→swinir` cascade and 17.3258 dB for SwinIR-Joint. Later exact-overlap audits found shared target pixels across the fixed train/validation partitions, so these historical values do not support independent generalization or future model selection. The local source/product lineage and calibrated signal domain remain unverified; the documented 256→128 degradation and noisy pseudo-target are representation-domain. SAR-CDL and the IGARSS 2025 program listing provide adjacent prior art, not validation of a local observation operator.

**Reason:** The long-term objective includes both cascade-versus-joint analysis and physics-constrained reconstruction. Leaving them implicit would omit core questions; promoting either route now would exceed the available evidence and violate the data/compute gates.

**Consequence:** Add H8/H9 to `research_hypotheses.md` with source-group, target, and compute prerequisites. Keep current model selection paused and test data inaccessible; no training or route promotion follows. See [the hypothesis register](research_hypotheses.md) and [current state](CURRENT_STATE.md).

## D-2026-10-19-32 — Record SAR-SR structure/speckle two-stage prior art

**Decision:** Record Lee and Son's MONTI 2026 workshop paper as ordered two-stage SAR-SR prior art and narrow the restoration-order gap. Do not treat it as a matched joint-versus-cascade result or as evidence for optical guidance.

**Evidence:** The indexed OpenReview manuscript describes structural restoration followed by conditional latent-diffusion speckle synthesis, with a blind-spot denoiser bridging real LR inputs and HR targets. It defines separate FWD structure and speckle measurements and reports comparison with single-stage baselines. The official [MONTI 2026 site](https://sites.google.com/view/monti2026/home) lists the paper as accepted and states that accepted workshop papers are non-archival. Direct OpenReview PDF access redirected to browser verification; full split/training details and code availability remain unverified. The method is single-modality, and no reversed SR/despeckling-order comparison or matched joint-restoration baseline is established by the reviewed evidence.

**Reason:** This paper makes a broad claim that no ordered two-stage SAR-SR comparison exists inaccurate. H8 remains relevant as a project-specific, fixed-input, fixed-target comparison among SR→despeckling, despeckling→SR, cascaded, and jointly optimized models with SAR fidelity guardrails.

**Consequence:** Update the related-work matrix, literature review, research-gaps note, H8, and current state. Preserve all data/compute gates: no local data, test measurements, training, or architecture selection occurred; B1 remains failed and B2 gated. See the [literature review](literature_review.md#diffusion-beyond-denoising), [research gaps](research_gaps.md), [hypothesis register](research_hypotheses.md), and [current state](CURRENT_STATE.md).

## D-2026-10-19-33 — Separate restoration order from training coupling in H8

**Decision:** Define the prospective H8 cascade comparison as a 2×2 design: `D→SR` and `SR→D`, each trained stage-wise and end-to-end, plus a direct-joint control. Treat task order and training coupling as separate factors.

**Evidence:** The H8 question compares ordered restoration with jointly optimized reconstruction. A single end-to-end cascade variant would confound order with training coupling. The simplified operator derivation in the [restoration-order analysis](restoration_order_analysis.md) shows why order can affect bias and propagated noise, while explicitly making no prediction about which order wins and no claim about the local PNG noise process.

**Reason:** The distinction is necessary to interpret a future matched comparison. Without both cascade orderings at both training couplings, a result could not be attributed to restoration order independently of end-to-end optimization.

**Consequence:** Update the H8 register, master plan, next actions, and current state. This is protocol refinement only; source-group/target provenance and compute prerequisites remain unresolved. No run, model selection, or test-data access occurred, and B1/B2 gates are unchanged.

## D-2026-10-19-34 — Keep OSdataset as an unadopted representation-domain candidate

**Decision:** Record OSdataset as a possible external Track-A source for controlled synthetic degradation, but do not adopt it as a calibrated SAR benchmark, clean-reference dataset, or replacement for the local 2k development set.

**Evidence:** The author [dataset repository](https://github.com/xym2009/OSdataset) describes 20 GaoFen-3/Google Earth parent scene pairs, 2,673 registered 512×512 pairs, and 10,692 256×256 pairs. It states that SAR amplitude is normalized to 0–255 and then `imadjust`-enhanced before 8-bit storage, and declares a CC-BY-NC license. The reviewed repository has only a README and download links; it exposes no patch-to-parent-scene crosswalk, acquisition dates, or group split. Google's [Geo Guidelines](https://about.google/brand-resource-center/products-and-services/geo-guidelines/) allow attributed research/education use, while its [Maps/Earth Additional Terms](https://www.google.com/intl/en-US/help/terms_maps/) restrict redistribution, copying, and bulk download, subject to stated exceptions. The author README does not identify exact optical providers/capture methods or explain how the terms apply to its archive. Direct IEEE article access required JavaScript verification, so this turn did not review the full paper.

**Reason:** The author-reported parent-scene count and high-resolution registered pairs make OSdataset a possible external representation-domain candidate. Missing crop grouping, acquisition timing, exact archive/version, and source-term reconciliation prevent a leakage-safe split or a defensible real-radiometry claim.

**Consequence:** Add the candidate and its adoption prerequisites to the literature review, roadmap, risk register, README, current state, and next actions. No dataset files were downloaded or opened, and no local test data, model, metric, or gate was accessed or changed. The original local provenance block remains open; B1 remains failed and B2 gated.

## D-2026-10-19-35 — Resolve imagery rights before accessing OSdataset archive

**Decision:** Do not download or adopt the OSdataset archive while the authorization to redistribute its Google Earth-derived imagery is unresolved.

**Evidence:** Google's official [Geo Guidelines](https://about.google/brand-resource-center/products-and-services/geo-guidelines/) permit properly attributed research/education use without advance permission, and describe limited non-commercial uses of static images. The [Google Maps/Earth Additional Terms](https://www.google.com/intl/en-US/help/terms_maps/) prohibit redistribution or bulk download of Maps content and limit copying to specifically permitted uses or applicable law. The OSdataset author repository describes the optical source as Google Earth and claims a CC-BY-NC dataset license, but the README does not identify specific providers, capture method, attribution records, or a rights basis for redistribution. The applicability of the Google terms to this archive is unresolved; this is not a legal determination.

**Reason:** A repository-level license cannot establish that the dataset author had rights to sublicense all underlying optical imagery. Downloading the archive before this is resolved would not be a justified data audit.

**Consequence:** Add authoritative Google policy sources to the dataset review and risks; require a documented rights path before acquisition or use. No archive was downloaded, and project data, metrics, and experiment gates remain unchanged.

## D-2026-10-19-36 — Keep QXS cache lineage and source groups unresolved

**Decision:** Keep the project-labeled local subset and the sibling QXS-named cache distinct from the official QXS-SAROPT release until an authorized version/crosswalk is established. Do not use crop-overlap geometry, numeric IDs, cache-folder labels, or guessed city assignments as source groups.

**Evidence:** The [primary QXS-SAROPT paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2103.08259) describes three single-polarization 1 m Gaofen-3 spotlight scenes and Google Earth optical imagery attributed to Maxar Technologies and INEGI. For 256-pixel patches, its statement “stride 52” conflicts with its stated 20% overlap under conventional step-size meaning: 52-pixel step implies 79.7% overlap, while a 204/205-pixel step yields a 51/52-pixel overlap. Local 204/205-pixel translations therefore fit the nominal 20% overlap but do not fingerprint the source. The [maintainer response to issue #3](https://github.com/yaoxu008/QXS-SAROPT/issues/3) says city-to-patch labels were not made; [issue #4](https://github.com/yaoxu008/QXS-SAROPT/issues/4) says the raw SAR scenes cannot be shared by the authors without source-center consent. The [official repository](https://github.com/yaoxu008/QXS-SAROPT) was rechecked on 2026-10-24: it still lists only its README and project image, and the [Releases page](https://github.com/yaoxu008/QXS-SAROPT/releases) has no releases. [Issue #13](https://github.com/yaoxu008/QXS-SAROPT/issues/13) remains open without a maintainer reply. The repository exposes no crosswalk. The local pixel audit matches 1,626 of 1,800 fixed train/validation pairs to a sibling QXS-named cache, but that cache remains Git-ignored and lacks upstream version/license/source-group metadata. The other 174 cache `test/` matches are filename-only; their payloads were not opened.

**Reason:** Sample-level pixel equivalence to a local cache and compatible crop geometry cannot establish the official release identity or original source groups. The author issue history also confirms that the public QXS release does not offer the needed city mapping, while the original SAR scenes are not available through the author repository.

**Consequence:** Update the data-source review, risks, README, current state, and next actions; preserve all local splits/results and B1/B2 status. Continue only if a new authorized archive/version or independently verifiable source mapping becomes available. No imagery, archive, test payload, metric, or model was accessed or changed in this audit.

## D-2026-10-19-37 — Keep 3MOS and SOMA-1M as alignment prior art

**Decision:** Record 3MOS and SOMA-1M as relevant multi-source/alignment resources, not as evidence for SAR-output restoration or substitutes for the local source-group mapping. Do not claim generic multi-source alignment or misalignment-aware fusion as new; keep the narrower residual-error effect on SAR reconstruction and SAR-only fallback untested.

**Evidence:** The 2025 [3MOS version of record](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44267-025-00091-0) describes 113k pairs from 11 regions/five SAR satellites and eight scenes. It uses 256×256 crops at 50% overlap and says the remaining cropped samples are randomly split 6:2:2; source-scene-disjoint membership is not specified. Its author [repository](https://github.com/3M-OS/3MOS) says the split filename lists are organized by satellite and scene, but list membership was not inspected and this does not establish source-group separation. The repository labels the dataset CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and names third-party source terms. Its April 2024 [arXiv v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.00838) differs in its construction summary (six satellites/14 original image pairs); use the version of record for published counts. The 2026 [SOMA-1M preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05480) reports 1.3M aligned pairs and a 100k training subset for matching, fusion, cloud removal, and SAR-to-optical translation. Its public [author repository](https://github.com/PeihaoWu/SOMA-1M) currently lists a README, links a test dataset, and says other subsets are being released progressively subject to third-party terms. Neither source evaluates restored-SAR fidelity, joint SAR despeckling/SR, or SAR-only fallback.

**Reason:** Alignment and correspondence benchmarks constrain broad novelty claims, but registration quality does not establish that optical is a useful or safe prior for SAR intensity reconstruction. 3MOS's random post-crop split is not evidence of source-group independence, and SOMA-1M's training release and dataset-specific rights are not currently verifiable from the author repository.

**Consequence:** Add both sources to the literature and risk records, keep them as adjacent prior art, and do not download or adopt them as restoration data without verifiable training files, source-group metadata, target semantics, and applicable rights. No local data, archives, test imagery, experiments, or metrics were accessed; B1 remains failed and B2 remains gated.

## D-2026-10-22-09 — Retain the narrow GNLM mismatch boundary

**Decision:** Treat GNLM as established prior art for statistically calibrated, SAR-domain rejection of optical-guided patch predictors and for one qualitative temporal/content-mismatch case. Do not describe that case as geometric-shift robustness or a learned whole-image fallback.

**Evidence:** The complete author manuscript is accessible through the official [arXiv HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/1811.11872v1); the arXiv record links DOI `10.1109/TGRS.2019.2906412`. It models intensity observations with unit-mean Gamma speckle and calibrates a Neyman–Pearson threshold on normalized patch log-ratio distance under an equal-signal assumption. Its T-SAR mismatch example compares 2008 SAR with 2009 post-demolition optical and 2002 pre-demolition optical guides; reported comparison is visual, and the paper describes manual registration without residual-offset measurements.

**Reason:** This precedent constrains novelty claims about local optical rejection and stale-content handling, while its despeckling-only task and unquantified natural temporal mismatch leave a narrower joint SAR SR/residual-geometry question open for future evidence.

**Consequence:** Keep B1 failed, B2 gated, and training deferred. No local data, metrics, test artifacts, model runs, or gates changed. The method details and boundaries are in [literature review](literature_review.md#optical-guided-sar-despeckling-and-predictor-reliability), [research risks](RESEARCH_RISKS.md), and [next actions](NEXT_ACTIONS.md).


## D-2026-10-22-10 — Classify Amieva normalization as preprocessing-level test-distribution use

**Decision:** Based on the indexed institutional published-version text, classify Amieva et al.'s whole-image-set percentile normalization before image-level splitting as preprocessing-level use of held-out image distribution statistics. Do not characterize it as training on test labels, test-metric checkpoint selection, or proven outcome leakage. Keep the complete methods review open.

**Evidence:** A targeted search index exposes p. 1399, §§3.3–3.4: per-band 0.1th/99.9th percentile values are computed across the entire image set for input and reference data, then entire images are assigned to train, validation, and test. An indexed Table 3 excerpt reports 5 training images/435,874 patches, 2 validation images/244,786 patches, and 3 full-image test scenes. The frozen local v2 protocol instead uses `uint8/255`, fixed `log1p(20x)/log1p(20)` normalization, unit clipping, and no cohort-wide percentile computation in its preparation code. Direct institutional PDF retrieval returned 403/timeout and the publisher route returned 403/cache miss; exact pooling or separation of Amieva's input/reference statistics could not be checked. These are indexed primary-text excerpts, not a direct full-text review. Sources: [institutional published-version record](https://academica-e.unavarra.es/entities/publication/c0c0e6a8-7084-423e-b803-198ef716aee8), [indexed bitstream](https://academica-e.unavarra.es/server/api/core/bitstreams/05cc73a9-ba52-4b8c-af6e-8c51d8011f28/content), [local v2 protocol](../../protocols/sen12_scene_dev1800_v2/b1_revalidation_v1.md), and [preprocessing implementation](../../scripts/prepare_fixed_degradation.py).

**Reason:** The excerpt establishes normalization-before-split ordering, but not which statistic pools were used or whether test labels influenced training or model selection. The evidence supports a narrow preprocessing caveat and no stronger leakage claim.

**Consequence:** Update the literature review, related-work matrix, risk register, and current-state caveat. Keep Amieva et al. as SAR-only joint-restoration prior art, disclose its three-scene test protocol and preprocessing-level test-distribution use, and distinguish its scaling from the frozen local v2 representation transform. No local experiment, model route, B1/B2 gate, test-data access, or method claim changed. See [literature review](literature_review.md), [related-work matrix](related_work_matrix.csv), [research risks](RESEARCH_RISKS.md), and [next actions](NEXT_ACTIONS.md).

## D-2026-10-23-24 — Classify MEOW as registration-only prior art

**Decision:** Record Bertrand et al.'s 2025 MEOW study as prior art for multiseason SAR–optical navigation registration and controlled registration degradation. Do not use it as evidence for SAR restoration quality, optical utility in JDSR, local v2 co-registration, or SAR-only fallback.

**Evidence:** The institutional publication listing confirms the paper's title, authors, venue, year, DOI, and HAL record. The HAL manuscript route was blocked in this review; the accessible co-author-uploaded manuscript describes MEOW, its matching-rate evaluation, blur/speckle conditions, temporal/geographic protocols, and limitations. The associated author GitHub repository and MEOW generation repository were inspected at README/metadata level, and the pinned model wrapper source was inspected directly: it samples Gamma(shape=L, rate=L), adds `20 log10(sample)` to SAR, clips to [-25, 5], then standardizes. The manuscript's main text and figure caption disagree on the east/west train/test direction; the temporal protocol reuses geography across years.

**Boundary:** No local data, model output, test imagery, or measurements were accessed. No experiment, protocol, gate, data adoption, or manuscript claim changed. The wrapper source does not establish physical validity of the implemented speckle transform or its lineage to the paper's reported tables; dataset/source terms were not audited.

**Consequence:** Keep local residual alignment unverified and retain the current source-matched nominal-georegistration wording. Any restoration stress test remains subject to the unchanged B1 prerequisite. See the [literature review](literature_review.md#optical-sar-registration-literature-and-scope-boundary) and [related-work matrix](related_work_matrix.csv).


## D-2026-10-23-25 — Keep GUSO as registration-only prior art

**Decision:** Record GUSO/FHReg as ultra-high-resolution SAR–optical registration prior art. Do not adopt GUSO as a SAR restoration benchmark or use its registration results as evidence for the local cohort's alignment, restoration fidelity, or optical fallback.

**Evidence:** The 2026 publisher preview reports 593,335 SAR–optical pairs from 319 cities across 78 countries at 0.16–0.98 m resolution and registration RMSE results. The author [repository README](https://github.com/vision-heng/GUSO) routes dataset access through a form and states academic-only use, prohibits commercial use, and requires prior written consent for derivative development or modification. The GitHub MIT label applies to repository code; the dataset terms are stated separately. No archive, split membership, or source-group metadata was inspected; the full article was not retrievable through this review route.

**Boundary:** No form was submitted and no data were downloaded. No local data, test imagery, metrics, model, experiment, or gate were accessed or changed. GUSO's registration results concern a very different spatial scale and do not provide a SAR restoration target or a measured fallback result.

**Consequence:** Keep GUSO in the registration literature and risk register only. Any future use requires a specific academic registration purpose, authorized access, review of source/provider terms and source-group splits, and an explicit plan for the resolution-domain gap. See the [literature review](literature_review.md#optical-sar-registration-literature-and-scope-boundary) and [research gaps](research_gaps.md).

No data/code were requested or retrieved; no local data, images, measurements, model, experiment, or gate were accessed or changed.

**Consequence:** Keep the prior-art classification and unresolved inference path in the literature review, matrix, research gaps, diffusion note, risks, current state, and next actions. Do not claim novelty for optical-guided SAR despeckling or diffusion-generated cross-domain references from this project. Joint SAR SR and controlled-mismatch fallback remain separate open questions.

## D-2026-10-23-36 — Record a possible C2 objective/metric tension without retuning

**Decision:** Do not extend or retune the sealed C2 runs on the same cohort. Treat the logged training/selection divergence as a plausible explanation to carry into future protocol design, not as a verified cause of B1 failure.

**Evidence:** The three captured C2 configs use `lambda_rec=1.0` and train-only calibrated `lambda_residual` values `0.739917531104381`, `0.8083524623361836`, and `0.7715829062386483` for seeds 0/1/2; each matches its calibration record. All direct SSIM, edge, guard, gate, and other optional losses are zero. The backbone remains frozen for the ten configured epochs. The model-selection score is `PSNR + 5·SSIM − 2·|log(edge_ratio)| − |log(TBR_mean_ratio)|`; recomputation from every epoch's logged values matches the recorded score, and each seed's best epoch is 1. From epoch 1 to 10 in all three seeds, validation total loss decreases while validation SSIM and selection score decrease; residual-contribution RMS increases. No prediction payload, input payload, or test result was read in this training-log diagnostic.

**Boundary:** The logs show metric divergence during optimization, not its mechanism. Possible explanations include the reconstruction/residual objective, model adaptation, representation-domain target noise, or nominal registration error. The current proxy target cannot identify which explanation controls clean-SAR quality.

**Consequence:** Keep the B1 decision unchanged. Resolve source/target and registration provenance before any new model experiment; a future protocol must align its predeclared loss design with its full metric gate and use a new justified development condition.

The inspected public materials do not explain whether positive coordinates are independently surveyed or generated by coordinate rules. See the [follow-up audit note](../../experiments/data_audits/sen12_sift_tiepoint_probe_20261023_v1/report.md), [dataset repository](https://github.com/YuChuang1205/SEN1-2-patch-dataset), [RRL-Net repository](https://github.com/YuChuang1205/RRL-Net), and [author homepage](https://yuchuang1205.github.io/).

**Boundary:** This is a bounded public-repository inspection, not proof that no separate generator exists. The full FIL-Net article method remains unreviewed. No `finally_test.txt` contents, images, measurements, models, metrics, protocol, or gate were accessed or changed.

**Consequence:** The zero-offset labels remain non-independent and cannot quantify the fall cohort's residual alignment. Keep P2 acquisition and fine-registration evidence open; do not repeat this route without a new access path or source artifact. B1 remains `not_promoted`; B2/B3 remain gated.


## D-2026-10-23-41 — Keep SEN12TP as a conditional provenance/timing candidate

**Decision:** Retain SEN12TP as a candidate source for a future, separate prospective development protocol; do not adopt or download it yet, and do not use it to reinterpret the local B1 result.

**Evidence:** The primary article and Zenodo record report 2,319 S1/S2 pairs over 1,236 areas, acquisition timestamps and ROI IDs in metadata, a maximum 12-hour pair gap, and spatially disjoint ROI construction. The article reports an 80/10/10 spatial train/validation/test split, while Zenodo describes a ~90/10 train/test release; exact archive-to-split membership is unverified. The author loader expects user-supplied ROI-directory splits but does not enforce grouping of repeated scene folders by `roi_id`. The dataset has no clean SAR target, spans ~222 GB uncompressed, and its rendered Zenodo license field is blank; the record prose says four train archives while the file listing shows five. See the [candidate audit](../../experiments/literature_audits/sen12tp_candidate_20261023_v1/report.md), [primary paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/s41064-023-00238-y), [Zenodo record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7342060), and [author loader](https://github.com/oceanites/sen12tp).

**Boundary:** Only publication, dataset landing-page, README, and public code text were reviewed. A search result exposed one article-level aggregate test-metric text while checking the split method; it was not used. No dataset test identity, image, or raw measurement file was accessed. The exact license, released split mapping, and main-branch commit remain unresolved. No model, protocol, gate, or local project test-access status changed. See the audit [access manifest](../../experiments/literature_audits/sen12tp_candidate_20261023_v1/access_manifest.json).

**Consequence:** Continue P2 source review. Before any acquisition, establish dataset rights and archive membership; if cleared, audit train-side metadata by `roi_id` and define a controlled representation-domain task with noisy pseudo-target limits. Keep test assets unopened and B2/B3 gated.

## D-2026-10-23-43 — Record image-level B1 v2 metric directions without changing the gate

**Decision:** Record the per-image direction counts as exploratory failure analysis of the already-sealed current-source B1 v2 validation results. Keep the frozen gate not_promoted; do not select a subgroup, retune, repeat the screen, or enter B2/B3 on this basis.

**Evidence:** The paired validation CSV's byte count and SHA-256 match aggregate_manifest.json; the run and aggregate manifests report candidate-test enumeration/access/use flags as false. Among 200 identities, the three-seed image-mean PSNR delta was favorable for 129 (106 favorable in every seed and 45 unfavorable in every seed). SSIM was unfavorable for 192 image means, and edge-strength ratio error increased for all 200 identities in every seed. The top 40 identities contributed 61.4% of the positive PSNR-delta sum. The canonical aggregate's source-group bootstrap intervals and gate arithmetic were not recomputed. See the [audit report](../../experiments/diagnostics/b1_v2_per_image_heterogeneity_20261023_v1/report.md), [analysis script](../../experiments/diagnostics/b1_v2_per_image_heterogeneity_20261023_v1/analyze.py), and [canonical aggregate report](../../experiments/sen12_scene_dev1800_b1_revalidation_20261023_source_aligned_v1/aggregate/report.md).

**Boundary:** This uses validation metric rows only; no images, arrays, predictions, or test measurements were accessed. Identities are nested in 15 source groups, targets are normalized PNG-derived noisy pseudo-targets, and fine co-registration is unverified. Direction counts do not establish clean-SAR utility, generalization, or a causal failure mechanism.

**Consequence:** Keep H1 unresolved and the tested C2 configuration not promoted. The next useful action remains source/target/acquisition provenance work; GPU training is also unavailable in the current shell until a new driver preflight succeeds. Preserve B2/B3 gating.

## D-2026-10-23-48 — Treat C2 objective/metric divergence as diagnostic, not causal

**Decision:** Keep the completed B1 v2 C2 result and gate unchanged. Do not retune losses, unfreeze the backbone, select a subgroup, or enter B2/B3 from this same cohort.

Only reconstruction and train-calibrated high-frequency residual losses are active; direct SSIM, edge, gate, and guard losses are zero, and the SAR backbone is frozen for all ten epochs. The run-bound loss source matches current code; two model/trainer hashes differ only after the separately recorded D-2026-10-23-46 interface maintenance. **Consequence:** Preserve the failed gate and current research stop at B1. Resume with provenance and source/target-independence work; any later model-selection route requires a new valid prospective split and a predeclared protocol.

**Consequence:** Remove generic gradient-registration and affine/flow-alignment novelty from candidate claims. Keep the project's unresolved question focused on downstream SAR-output fidelity and target-free optical utility/rejection after valid B1 evidence and source/target provenance are available.

## D-2026-10-24-14 — Keep C2 stopped after residual diagnosis

**Decision:** Keep the B1 v2 C2 gate `not_promoted`; do not enter B2/B3, retrain, or adopt global residual rescaling from this diagnostic. Classify the actual residual evidence as mixed and inconclusive.

Per-seed labels are D/D/A and the aggregate is D. See the [diagnostic report](../../experiments/diagnostics/b1_v2_c2_actual_residual_diagnostic_20261024_v1/report.md) and [registry entry](EXPERIMENT_REGISTRY.md#b1-v2-c2-actual-residual-diagnostic-2026-10-24-validation-only).

The diagnostic used the checkpoint's saved 5/1.0 high-pass configuration; D-2026-10-23-46 records unchanged default behavior after the interface repair. ## D-2026-10-24-15 — Keep C2 gate activation as a bounded composite-score rank cue

**Decision:** Record bounded support for the frozen C2 model's mean gate activation as a rank cue for per-image actual-minus-base strict-score changes on this validation cohort. Do not call it calibrated reliability, set a threshold, select identities/checkpoints, alter the B1 gate, or enter B2/B3.

**Evidence:** The zero-training analysis paired input-derived gate_activation_mean with per-image selection_score changes for the same 200 names and seeds 0/1/2. Seed-wise Spearman rho values were +0.8675, +0.8590, and +0.8383; their mean was +0.8549, with a 95% cluster-bootstrap interval [+0.7259,+0.9107] from 10,000 draws resampling 15 source folders. All three seeds were positive and the interval cleared zero, satisfying the predeclared bounded-support rule. Per-seed rho values for ΔPSNR (+0.2287, +0.1428, −0.2063) and ΔSSIM (−0.0652, +0.0389, −0.1548) were weak or inconsistent. Per-image strict_score is PSNR + 5·SSIM − 2·|ln(edge_strength_ratio)| − |ln(tbr_mean_ratio)| in [OGSRN/metrics.py](../../OGSRN/metrics.py#L55); this analysis does not attribute the association to one component.

**Boundary:** This is an association on repeatedly used development validation, with normalized PNG-derived noisy pseudo-targets, fine registration unverified, and 15 folders that are not verified parent-scene/acquisition IDs. The prior C2 aggregate result still fails the frozen B1 gate. The result establishes no causal reliability, clean-SAR utility, per-metric safety, or generalization. No test measurements, training, model selection, gate change, or B2/B3 work occurred. See the [diagnostic record](../../experiments/diagnostics/b1_v2_c2_gate_utility_alignment_20261024_v1/).

**Consequence:** Keep the association as a candidate for prospective validation only. Do not threshold or retune this same cohort. Return to source/version and parent-scene/target/registration provenance before any new model-selection or training work; B1 remains not_promoted, B2/B3 gated.

## D-2026-10-25-08 — Record MD-Glow as SAR multi-task despeckling/SR prior art

## D-2026-10-25-10 — Quantify input-target dependence under an idealized stack model

**Decision:** Require explicit acquisition-stack membership before describing a multitemporal reference as independent of its noisy input. Use the correlation calculation only as a conditional theoretical sensitivity, not as a measurement of a released dataset.

**Evidence:** If intensity observations follow `I_i=ρS_i` for a static reflectivity `ρ`, with independent unit-mean speckle `S_i` of variance `1/L`, and the paired input `I_1` is included in an `N`-image mean `T_N`, then `Cov(I_1−ρ,T_N−ρ | ρ)=ρ²/(NL)` and the conditional noise-residual correlation is `1/√N`. It is zero if the input is excluded and all target acquisitions are independent. Thus inclusion would give correlation 0.447–0.200 for `N=5…25` under the assumptions. The linked 2024 Toronto [reference-generation code](https://github.com/rubenchov/SAR_despeckling_dataset/blob/main/3.%20Generate_GTruth.py) and [pairing code](https://github.com/rubenchov/SAR_despeckling_dataset/blob/main/4.%20Clip_Image.py) establish that its August 24 input contributes to its ten-date average. The 2026 [article](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dib.2026.112999) does not disclose per-reference acquisition membership.

**Boundary and consequence:** The derivation assumes a static scene, exact registration, equal looks, and independent speckle; it does not establish the actual 0–255 representation or dependence in either release. No dataset payload, local data, test data, experiment, selection, or gate changed. Keep the 2026 candidate unadopted until its stack map and metadata are available; B1 remains `not_promoted`, and B2/B3 remain gated.

## D-2026-10-25-12 — Bound the inverse moments of representation-domain Gamma noise

**Decision:** Continue to describe the prospective B1 v2 noise condition as a representation-domain composite stress test. Do not interpret its looks-2 Gamma multiplier as calibrated intensity speckle or a physical-domain likelihood, including after an inverse log transform.

**Evidence:** Source and protocol text establish `φ(x)=ln(1+20x)/ln(21)`, followed by filtering/downsampling and direct multiplication by `G~Gamma(L,L)` in representation space. For the resulting pre-speckle scalar `q`, `qG` has conditional mean `q` and variance `q²/L`. Under the separate assumption that the unclipped inverse `ψ(y)=(21ʸ−1)/20` is later applied, its conditional expectation exists only for `q ln(21)<L`; at `L=2`, it diverges for `q≥2/ln(21)≈0.657`. The second moment is finite only for `q<1/ln(21)≈0.328`. These are algebraic conditions, not measured properties of local inputs. See the [derivation audit](representation_domain_gamma_composition_20261025.md).

**Boundary and consequence:** No data, test payload, metric, checkpoint, model, or experiment was accessed or changed; no tests were run. This adds no physical validation and does not change the frozen protocol or any gate. B1 remains `not_promoted`; B2/B3 remain gated. A physical-domain study remains contingent on authoritative calibrated-input metadata and a degradation defined before normalization.

## D-2026-10-25-19 — Distinguish absent-optical fallback from mismatch robustness

**Decision:** Describe MMCANetV2 as implementing a model-level absent-optical fallback to its SAR base. Do not describe the optional alignment field or structural gate as evidence that the model detects or safely rejects misregistered or semantically wrong optical input.

**Evidence:** The SAR base is SwinIRJoint with a sigmoid output. In MMCANetV2.forward, optical None creates an all-zero tensor and false presence mask; the residual is multiplied by that mask, so the clamped output equals the sigmoid-bounded SAR base. A zero optical tensor is also treated as absent unless optical_present overrides it. Optional alignment predicts a zero-initialized, per-pixel two-channel offset bounded by tanh times max_alignment_pixels and applies grid_sample. No direct offset labels or offset-smoothness term appear in the inspected trainer/loss source. When enabled, the structural gate target is derived from HR target/optical gradient magnitude and sign-invariant edge-direction agreement, not whether the residual improves restoration quality. See the [source audit](../../experiments/diagnostics/mmcanet_v2_architecture_source_audit_20261025_v1/report.md).

**Boundary:** These are source-level facts, not runtime or performance results. No data, test payload, checkpoint, model forward, experiment, metric, parameter/runtime profile, or historical gate changed. A separate potential test-associated text-exposure event from the preceding broad search is recorded at [this disclosure](../../experiments/data_audits/architecture_search_text_exposure_20261025_v1/report.md). B1 remains not_promoted; B2/B3 remain gated.

**Consequence:** Update claim language to credit the absent-optical interface path while keeping geometric mismatch detection, safe rejection, and optical utility untested. Preserve the B1/B2/B3 gates.
